key_insight: PaperBanana automates the end-to-end creation of publication-ready academic illustrations by orchestrating specialized agents powered by vision-language models and image generators, enabling iterative planning, rendering, and refinement with minimal human effort.
problem_solved: Reduces the time and expertise required to produce high-quality, publication-ready figures—currently a labor-intensive bottleneck in the research and autonomous AI scientist workflows.
method: Agent orchestration: specialized agents handle reference retrieval, content & style planning, image rendering, and iterative refinement.
Leverages state-of-the-art vision-language models (VLMs) and image generation models to translate scientific intent into polished visuals.
Automated quality and style control to align outputs with publication standards and researcher preferences.
impact: Speeds up manuscript preparation and lowers the barrier for researchers to produce consistent, high-quality figures, enabling faster dissemination and reproducibility in AI/ML research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing agent orchestration from reference retrieval → planning → rendering → iterative refinement
Before/after examples of raw sketches or data plots vs. publication-ready illustrations
Component icons for VLM, image generator, and quality-control agent with brief callouts
A small flowchart showing human-in-the-loop checkpoints and automated style compliance
paper_title: PaperBanana: Automating Academic Illustration for AI Scientists
paper_authors: Dawei Zhu, Rui Meng, Yale Song, Xiyu Wei, Sujian Li
